verses.english: “Mendicants, a mendicant should live mindful and aware.
This is my instruction to you.
And how is a mendicant mindful?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sato hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant is mindful.
And how is a mendicant aware?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno viditā vedanā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṁ gacchanti.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant knows feelings as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away.

verses.pali: Viditā vitakkā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṁ gacchanti.
verses.english: They know thoughts as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away.

verses.pali: Viditā saññā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṁ gacchanti.
verses.english: They know perceptions as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sampajāno hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant is aware.
A mendicant should live mindful and aware.
This is my instruction to you.”
